![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077122/assets/c51295239ec195b494cfc67e295c50a7f1a9464bc0d24e32d53fb624f311cfdd.png)

Find the parametric equations of the hyperbola shown above given that its asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{1}{2}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

The vertices of the hyperbola occur at $(\pm a,0).$ From the graph, we have that $(2,0)$ is a vertex of the hyperbola, so $a=2.$

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.$ In our case, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{1}{2}x,$ and so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{b}{a} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{b}{2} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the hyperbola are

$$
x=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$
